security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU allows S-mode or U-mode access to stopei, eip[k], or eie[k] CSRs when Smstateen is implemented and mstateen0 bit 58 (IMSIC) is zero, without raising an illegal instruction exception. This occurs if the CSR read/write handler for these CSRs does not check the mstateen0[58] state-enable bit before permitting access from lower privilege levels.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: csr_ops handler for stopei/eip/eie missing mstateen0 bit-58 check before s-mode/u-mode access; or mstateen0 CSR definition missing bit 58 as a writable/readable field when Smstateen is present
security_spec.summary: mstateen0 bit 58 gates S/U-mode access to ACLIC CSRs reused from IMSIC (stopei/eip/eie); QEMU must raise illegal instruction exception when bit 58 is zero, else lower-privilege guest code bypasses state-enable access control

findings.finding: The predicate for siselect/sireg CSRs checks only ext_smaia/ssaia/sscsrind/smcsrind presence and S-mode, but performs NO smstateen_acc_ok() check for SMSTATEEN0_AIA (bit 59) or SMSTATEEN0_IMSIC (bit 58). When ext_smstateen is enabled, S-mode can access these CSRs even when mstateen0 bit 59/58 is zero, bypassing the state-enable gate.

The rmw_xireg handler checks smstateen_acc_ok(SMSTATEEN0_SVSLCT) at line 2889, which controls srmcfg/ssqosid CSRIND access. When iselect is in the AIA/IMSIC range (xiselect_aia_range is true), it dispatches to rmw_xireg_aia without checking SMSTATEEN0_AIA or SMSTATEEN0_IMSIC. This means S-mode can read/write eip[k] (iselect 0x80-0xbf), eie[k] (iselect 0xc0-0xff), eidelivery (iselect 0x70), and eithreshold (iselect 0x72) through sireg even when mstateen0[58] (IMSIC) is zero.

When iselect falls in the IMSIC range (ISELECT_IMSIC_FIRST to ISELECT_IMSIC_LAST), rmw_xireg_aia directly calls the IMSIC emulation callback via env->aia_ireg_rmw_fn[priv] without any smstateen_acc_ok() check for SMSTATEEN0_IMSIC. This is the actual IMSIC register access point that lacks the smstateen guard — the check for CSR_SIREG at line 2663-2669 only guards against MIP_SEIP delegation bypass, not smstateen.

The VS-mode predicate for vsiselect/vsireg has the same missing-smstateen-check bug as csrind_or_aia_smode. When ext_smstateen is implemented, a guest VS-mode can access vsireg to reach IMSIC registers without SMSTATEEN0_IMSIC being checked, bypassing the hypervisor's ability to restrict guest IMSIC access via hstateen0/sstateen0 masking.

STOPEI is properly guarded: aia_smode calls smstateen_acc_ok(env, 0, SMSTATEEN0_IMSIC) when csrno == CSR_STOPEI (line 362). S-mode access to stopei is correctly blocked when mstateen0 bit 58 is zero and ext_smstateen is implemented.
VSTOPEI is properly guarded: aia_hmode calls smstateen_acc_ok(env, 0, SMSTATEEN0_IMSIC) when csrno == CSR_VSTOPEI (line 713). VS-mode access to vstopei is correctly gated by the smstateen IMSIC bit.

mstateen0 bit 58 (SMSTATEEN0_IMSIC) is correctly defined as a writable field when ext_smaia is enabled (line 3479-3480). The wr_mask includes SMSTATEEN0_AIA | SMSTATEEN0_IMSIC. The read handler (read_mstateen) reads directly from env->mstateen[index]. The CSR field mask and read/write semantics are correct.

The smstateen_acc_ok helper itself is correctly implemented. It correctly exempts M-mode (line 52), checks mstateen, then checks hstateen for virtualized contexts, and finally sstateen for U-mode. The bug is in the call sites that fail to invoke this function, not in the function itself.
